# F001 FALSIFIER — Coherence pruning is semantically inverted
# The claim: pruning text to meet coherence budget INCREASES density because
# constraint_count comes from the static policy, not the text being pruned.
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering")

from bench.cdsfl_registry.composer import (
    _prune_for_coherence, DirectivePacket, _count_constraints, 
    _render_directive_text
)

# Create a policy with known constraint count
policy = {"constraints": {"a": True, "b": True, "c": True, "d": "required"}}
constraint_count = _count_constraints(policy)
print(f"Constraint count (from policy): {constraint_count}")

# Create packets with text well over budget — SOFT, prunable text
packets = [
    DirectivePacket(
        layer="universal", name="core", 
        text="CDSFL CORE MINIMAL\npolicy.constraints.a=true",
        constraint_class="HARD", tags=set()
    ),
    DirectivePacket(
        layer="situation", name="verbose_situation",
        text="This is a very long situation directive." * 50,  # ~2000 chars
        constraint_class="SOFT", tags={"situation"}
    ),
]

# Calculate pre-pruning metrics
total_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in packets)
token_estimate = max(total_chars // 4, 1)
pre_density = constraint_count / token_estimate
print(f"\nPre-pruning:")
print(f"  total_chars: {total_chars}")
print(f"  token_estimate: {token_estimate}")
print(f"  density: {constraint_count}/{token_estimate} = {pre_density:.6f}")

# Set a tight budget that's below the current density
budget = 0.001  # Very tight — will trigger pruning
print(f"  budget: {budget}")
print(f"  density > budget: {pre_density > budget}")

# Run pruning
pruned_packets, pruned_names = _prune_for_coherence(packets, policy, budget)
print(f"\nPost-pruning:")
print(f"  pruned_soft: {pruned_names}")

post_chars = sum(len(p.text) for p in pruned_packets)
post_tokens = max(post_chars // 4, 1)
post_density = constraint_count / post_tokens
print(f"  total_chars: {post_chars}")
print(f"  token_estimate: {post_tokens}")
print(f"  density: {constraint_count}/{post_tokens} = {post_density:.6f}")

# CRITICAL CHECK: Did density go UP (the bug) or DOWN (correct behavior)?
if post_density > pre_density:
    print(f"\nFALSIFIED: Density INCREASED from {pre_density:.6f} to {post_density:.6f}")
    print("The pruning algorithm is semantically inverted — it makes the problem WORSE.")
else:
    print(f"\nPASS: Density decreased from {pre_density:.6f} to {post_density:.6f}")
